title: Thanksgiving in Laredo: markets, free turkeys, tree lighting and two morning runs
excerpt: From a fall market and a free turkey giveaway to the ninth annual tree lighting and two Thanksgiving morning runs, Laredo has a full calendar of Thanksgiving-season events, according to KGNS.
content:
From a fall market and a free turkey giveaway to the ninth annual tree lighting and two Thanksgiving morning runs, Laredo has a full calendar of Thanksgiving-season events, according to KGNS.

The season opens with the BornToShop Fall Market on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Jardin Contreras, 811 Iturbide St., with vintage and Y2K jewelry, arts and crafts, home décor, food, plants and apparel. On Sunday, Nov. 15, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., the Martinez King Law Firm at 8917 Molly, Suite 2, hosts its annual turkey event, “A Season of Giving,” with turkeys available while supplies last.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 11:30 a.m., the Laredo Chamber of Commerce's Women in Business hosts “Friendsgiving: A Seat at Her Table” at El Capataz, 7220 NE Bob Bullock Loop, Suite C-7. The cost is $50 for members and $60 for nonmembers, with reservations required and space limited.

On Thursday, Nov. 19, from 7 to 9 p.m., BMG Xtreme Sports at 6420 Sinatra Parkway hosts Bike Night of Giving, with music, food and riders, partnering with Angels on Earth for a turkey and canned-food drive. Attendees are asked to bring donations.

On Friday, Nov. 20, at 6 p.m., the Outlet Shoppes at Laredo, 1600 Water St., hosts its ninth annual tree lighting outside Burlington near Coach, with Santa and Mrs. Claus, live music and vendors, hosted by KGNS. On Saturday, Nov. 21, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., the El Centro de Laredo Farmers Market returns to the Outlet Shoppes, hosted by Laredo Main Street, with produce, cooking demos, live music, folklórico and giveaways. EBT and SNAP are accepted, including Double Up Food Bucks.

Also on Saturday, Nov. 21, from 12:30 to 3:30 p.m., the Friendsgiving Lotería at Mesquite takes place at the Paisano Mesquite model home in Wright Ranch, hosted by Indoor Gardens Plant Shop and Paisano Homes, with plants, prizes and a meal of turkey, mashed potatoes and corn. The cost is $35 and includes two cards; seating is limited and reservations are required. From 1 to 5 p.m. the same day, the Gourd-geous Goods Pop-Up runs at the Crafty Atrium Pop-Up Shop at Embassy Suites by Hilton Laredo, 110 Calle del Norte. The shop is still seeking vendors, who should direct-message Crafty Atrium and must have a valid sales-tax number.

On Sunday, Nov. 22, from noon to 3 p.m., Embassy Suites hosts a Thanksgiving brunch buffet with a carving station, mashed potatoes, candied sweet potatoes, cranberry sauce, green-bean casserole, corn, stuffing, biscuits, desserts, mimosas and a Bloody Mary bar. The cost is $25 for adults, $20 for seniors, $18 for military and $12 for children.

On Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, Nov. 26, two runs take place. The 19th annual Gateway City Turkey Trot, a JRHAST 10K/5K run and walk benefiting people in need, starts at 8 a.m. at 603 Shiloh Drive. Registration is $25 through Nov. 14, $10 for students 18 and younger, $35 from Nov. 15 to 25, and $50 on race day, with packet pickup from 4 to 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Orangetheory Fitness, 3502 E Del Mar Blvd., Suite 6. The Guajolote 5K and 10K, Hamilton Trophies' 45th anniversary event at 1320 Garden St., has preregistration at 7 a.m. and races at 8:30 a.m. It is open to ages 4 and up, with children 12 and under accompanied by an adult. Free parking is available at LISD Shirley Field; strollers must stay at the back and pets are not permitted, with service-animal exceptions reviewed case by case.

Sources: KGNS, “Thanksgiving events in Laredo: Markets, meals and a turkey giveaway” (Nov. 12, 2026).
